subject: Retention and session-logging gap for BYOK Private deploy — triage
messages:
From: Danielle Morris <danielle.morris@clearspring.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: raj.patel@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-07-12 09:15 -0700
Subject: Missing SSO session ID in audit exports for private BYOK deployment

Hi Sean —

We're in the middle of an internal audit for ClearSpring's EU VPC deployment and noticed the audit export doesn't include the SSO session identifier (the SAML/OIDC session id) that our security team needs to link user sessions to tokens. They also requested retention of session-level logs for 12 months, and examples of key-management operations tied to customer CMKs (BYOK).

Could you confirm whether the private package emits a session id field in the audit logs, and whether there is an option to extend the retention window to 12 months for these events? If not, we need a mitigation plan (short-term: include application-level linking; medium-term: runtime change).

Attaching a short requirement doc and a sample log they exported.

Thanks,
Danielle
Operations Manager — ClearSpring Health

Attachments: audit_requirements_clearspring.pdf, sso-session-log-sample.txt

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: danielle.morris@clearspring.com
Date: 2027-07-12 10:02 -0700
Subject: RE: Missing SSO session ID in audit exports for private BYOK deployment

Thanks for the sample, Danielle — looping in Product (Marissa) and Platform (Priyom, Irene) to triage. Quick summary of asks from the audit:
- Make SSO session id available in audit export (per-session linkage)
- Retention: 12 months for session-level events and CMK operations
- Evidence: mapping of keystore operations to CMK IDs for BYOK customers

Initial questions for the team: 1) Is the session id captured anywhere today (application logs, auth proxy, runtime KV cache)? 2) What is the current max retention for private deployments (per tenant) and how disruptive is 12 months? 3) Any existing perf/size implications for keeping session-level logs that long?

Action: can each of you reply with short answers and suggested next steps by EOD so I can respond to ClearSpring with a roadmapped approach?

—Sean
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: danielle.morris@clearspring.com
Date: 2027-07-12 12:40 -0700
Subject: RE: Missing SSO session ID in audit exports for private BYOK deployment

Quick take from product:
- We don't currently include a dedicated SSO session id field in the runtime audit export. Auth is handled by a pluggable proxy in the private package; that proxy does have a session token but we don't surface it into the standard audit schema.
- Retention: Private deployments default to 90 days in our on-disk pipeline; we offer longer retention as a managed add-on for Dedicated but the private package left to customer infra means we haven't productized an automated 12-month extension.

Proposed short-term mitigation (48–72h):
1) We can add a lightweight connector in the auth proxy that copies the auth session id into the per-request metadata field in audit rows (config flag). This is low-risk and non-breaking.
2) For retention, propose a documented runbook: customers can configure their object store lifecycle to keep exported audit blobs for 12 months; we'll provide a retention_matrix_proposal.xlsx to guide settings and a small helper script.

Proposed medium-term (Q3 roadmap):
- Productize a config-driven 'session_id_export' toggle in the private control plane and a supported retention policy option up to 12 months. Estimate: 2 sprints (engineering + QA).

I'll put a short PRD and sample config in the drive link.

—Marissa
VP, Product — Redwood Inference

From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: danielle.morris@clearspring.com
Date: 2027-07-13 09:05 -0700
Subject: RE: Missing SSO session ID in audit exports for private BYOK deployment

Engineering/Platform notes:
- Where the session id currently exists: the auth proxy stores a transient session token; the serving runtime only sees an opaque auth header and a mapped user id. We can surface the proxy token into request metadata and persist it into the audit pipeline. Implementation risk: low.
- Retention & storage impact: keeping session-level logs for 12 months increases archive volume roughly ~6x based on ClearSpring's traffic profile (Danielle's sample). Cost impact for customers: potentially material if they use SSD-backed object store. We should publish cost guidance.

Short-term deliverables (this week):
- Small auth-proxy patch to emit session_id (configurable) + unit tests
- Helper script + retention_matrix_proposal.xlsx for customer self-service

Medium-term: add a 'retention_policy' option in private control plane to let customers select 90/180/365 days and an associated config validation check at install time. Estimate: 3 eng sprints + documentation.

I'll prepare a terse implementation plan and risk matrix.

—Priyom
Staff Engineer, Platform — Redwood Inference

From: irene.choi@redwood.com <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: danielle.morris@clearspring.com, raj.patel@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-07-13 13:18 -0700
Subject: RE: Missing SSO session ID in audit exports for private BYOK deployment

Operational considerations from Security & Compliance side:
- Keystore/CMK ops mapping: we can add CMK identifiers to audit rows for each keystore operation (rotate, export, sign). That is already in place for Dedicated; private package will need a tiny shim to capture the customer CMK-id from the keystore driver.
- Evidence packaging: recommend we provide a redacted evidence bundle (audit_requirements_clearspring.pdf) with schema mapping, sample logs, and a checklist to help ClearSpring satisfy their auditor.
- Short-term control: provide a signed attestation that runtime changes will be low-risk and include a rollback plan.

Next steps: 1) Priyom to drop a PR for the proxy flag and a test build by EOD. 2) Marissa to prepare PRD with timeline (2 sprints for config toggle; 3 sprints for retention). 3) Sean to coordinate an engineering-ops call with ClearSpring this week for timelines and to collect final audit evidence requirements.

—Irene
Head, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: danielle.morris@clearspring.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com, raj.patel@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-07-14 16:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Missing SSO session ID in audit exports for private BYOK deployment — next steps

Danielle — thanks for patience. Short timeline and deliverables:
- Today: Priyom will open a test build with a config flag that emits the SSO session token into audit rows. We'll share a build and instructions within 24 hours.
- 48–72h: Marissa/Irene will produce a short evidence bundle (schema, sample logs) and the retention_matrix_proposal.xlsx to help ClearSpring configure 12-month retention in their object store.
- Roadmap: product ticket to add 'session_id_export' toggle to private control plane (ETA: end of Q3) and retention policy selections (ETA: end of Q3).

Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to validate the sample build and confirm the auditor's checklist? Proposed: 2027-07-15 10:00 AM CET / 01:00 AM PDT — if that doesn't work, propose windows.

Thanks — I'll follow up with the Drive link to artifacts and a short demo build once Priyom's PR lands.

—Sean
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
